\begin{tablenotes}\footnotesize
\item \emph{Notes:} $\delta$ of \PaperRef{Table~2}{Table~\ref{tab:survival}}, all ten offices; each row changes one thing in the preferred specification. Earlier specification: firm size of the harmonised applicant alone, linear citation slopes by office, no grant-lag controls. Linear citation slopes: in place of citation bins. Alive 12 years after filing: outcome counted from filing, with the grant-lag controls. Reweighted: foreign patents weighted to the domestic citation-bin distribution of their office. Same-office citations: citations from applications filed at the same office, a narrower and noisier measure, in place of family citations. Identical fees: without Russia (separate non-resident fees until 2012), patents alive three years after grant (early-year discounts for domestic owners in China and Korea), Chinese grants to 2010 and Korean grants to 2006, so that domestic and foreign owners pay the same fees in every year the outcome covers. Full corporate group: adds links by brand words. Applicant-record country: drops owners whose country is imputed. Oster bound: coefficient if unobservables moved it as much, relative to their explanatory power, as the controls do ($\beta = 1$, $R_{\max} = 1.3 R^2$). Standard errors clustered by owner in parentheses. $^{*}$~$p<0.1$, $^{**}$~$p<0.05$, $^{***}$~$p<0.01$.
\end{tablenotes}
